title: Counting Principles and Probability
summary: The fundamental counting principle, factorial notation, arrangements with and without repetition, arrangements with conditions and identical items, and using counting to find probabilities.

notes.text: If one choice can be made in $m$ ways and a second independent choice in $n$ ways, the two together can be made in $m \times n$ ways.

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: A menu has 3 starters, 5 main meals and 2 desserts. How many different three-course meals are possible?

notes.caption: $n$ different objects can be arranged in a row in $n!$ ways

notes.title: Worked example 2
notes.problem: In how many ways can 6 learners stand in a line?

notes.title: Worked example 3: items kept together
notes.problem: In how many ways can the letters of the word FRIENDS be arranged if the vowels (I and E) must stay together?
steps: Treat 'IE' as one unit: 6 units can be arranged in $6!$ ways.
The vowels can be arranged within their unit in $2!$ ways.

notes.caption: Arrangements of $n$ objects where $a$ are identical, $b$ are identical, and so on

notes.title: Worked example 4
notes.problem: How many different arrangements are there of the letters of the word BANANA?
steps: 6 letters: A appears 3 times, N twice.

notes.latex: P(E) = \frac{\text{number of arrangements in which } E \text{ happens}}{\text{total number of arrangements}}

notes.title: Worked example 5
notes.problem: The letters of the word MATHS are arranged randomly. Find the probability that the arrangement starts with a vowel.

questions.prompt: A learner has 4 shirts, 3 pairs of trousers and 2 pairs of shoes. How many different outfits are possible?
How many 5-digit codes can be made from the digits 0 to 9 if digits may be repeated?
How many 3-letter arrangements can be made from the letters A, B, C, D, E, F if no letter may be repeated?
How many different arrangements are there of the letters of the word LETTER?
In how many ways can 5 boys and 3 girls sit in a row if the girls must sit together?
questions.memo:
✓ Treat girls as one unit: $6!$ (1)
✓ Girls among themselves: $3!$ (1)
✓ $720 \times 6 = 4\ 320$ (1)

questions.prompt: The letters of the word NUMBERS are arranged. How many arrangements begin and end with a consonant?
questions.memo:
✓ Consonants: N, M, B, R, S (5) (1)
✓ First and last: $5 \times 4 = 20$ (1)
✓ Middle: $5! = 120$, total $2\ 400$ (1)

questions.prompt: A 4-digit code is formed using the digits 1 to 9 without repetition. What is the probability that the code is an even number?
questions.memo:
✓ Total: $9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6 = 3\ 024$ (1)
✓ Last digit even: 4 choices (2, 4, 6, 8) (1)
✓ Even codes: $4 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6 = 1\ 344$ (1)
✓ $P = \frac{1\ 344}{3\ 024} = \frac{4}{9}$ (1)

questions.prompt: In how many ways can the letters of the word PENCIL be arranged so that the vowels are NOT next to each other?
